reasoning: Recent Florida Senate polling from the last 45 days shows Republicans ahead by roughly 7 to 10 points in head-to-head general-election matchups, with the most recent public poll giving Ashley Moody a 10-point lead over Alex Vindman. I did not find a state-specific Florida presidential general-election poll in the provided results, so the current race margin is best summarized from the Senate contest alone.

sources.name: University of North Florida Public Opinion Research Lab via PollsMax aggregate
sources.details: Public Opinion Research Lab at the University of North Florida found Ashley Moody leading Alex Vindman 50%-40% among 848 likely Florida midterm voters.

sources.name: Florida Phoenix / University of North Florida Poll
sources.details: Florida Phoenix reported the UNF poll showing Moody ahead of Vindman by 10 points in a general-election matchup.

sources.name: Tallahassee Democrat / University of North Florida Poll
sources.details: Tallahassee Democrat summarized the same UNF survey and said Moody led Vindman 50%-40%, a 10-point Republican margin.

sources.name: Politico Florida Playbook / University of North Florida Poll
sources.details: Politico's Florida Playbook noted the UNF poll showing Moody with a 10-point edge over Vindman.

sources.name: Pollsmax Florida Senate Polling Average
sources.details: Pollsmax's Florida Senate polling average showed Moody at 47.6% and Vindman at 40.6%, for a Republican lead of 7.0 points.

sources.name: Global Strategy Group Florida Senate Poll
sources.details: Global Strategy Group's Florida Senate survey found Ashley Moody ahead of Alex Vindman 46%-43% among likely voters, a 3-point Republican lead.

sources.name: Florida Politics summary of UNF Senate polling
sources.details: These reports all describe the Florida Senate race as Republican-leaning, with Moody leading by high single digits to low double digits.
